chunks: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:
"Do not curse the winds, for they are commanded, nor the mountains, nor the hours, nor the days, nor the nights, lest you commit sin and it returns to you."

key_terms.الرِّياحَ: the winds, as created forces acting by Allah’s command
key_terms.الْجِبالَ: the mountains, which should not be cursed
key_terms.يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْكُمْ: it returns to you, meaning the blame or sin comes back upon you

ai.seo_question: Why did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله forbid cursing the wind, days, and nights?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches believers not to curse created things such as the winds, mountains, times, days, and nights, because they operate under divine command. It warns that such speech is sinful and that its evil consequence returns to the speaker.
